result.task: Download the paper 'Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering'. How many formulas are in the article and which one is the loss function?
result.final_answer:
I have all the information I need. Let me provide my final answer.

## Summary of Findings

**Paper Downloaded:** "Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering" by Vladimir Karpukhin, Barlas Oğuz, Sewon Min, Patrick Lewis, Ledell Wu, Sergey Edunov, Danqi Chen, Wen-tau Yih (Facebook AI / University of Washington / Princeton University), arXiv:2004.04906v3.

I accessed both the PDF (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.04906) and the HTML version (https://arxiv.org/html/2004.04906v3) to inspect the paper's contents.

## Number of Formulas

The paper contains **3 displayed/numbered equations** (5 individually-numbered equations if you count each line in the aligned group separately):

| Eq. # | Section | Formula | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|---------|
| (1) | §3.1 Overview | sim(q, p) = E_Q(q)ᵀ E_P(p) | Similarity (dot-product) function between question and passage encoders |
| (2) | §3.2 Training | L(q_i, p_i⁺, p_i,1⁻, …, p_i,n⁻) = −log[ e^sim(q_i,p_i⁺) / (e^sim(q_i,p_i⁺) + Σⱼ e^sim(q_i,p_i,j⁻)) ] | **Loss function** (negative log-likelihood) |
| (3) | §6.1 End-to-end QA | P_start,i(s) = softmax(P_i w_start)_s | Reader start-position probability |
| (4) | §6.1 End-to-end QA | P_end,i(t) = softmax(P_i w_end)_t | Reader end-position probability |
| (5) | §6.1 End-to-end QA | P_selected(i) = softmax(P̂ᵀ w_selected)_i | Reader passage-selection probability |

(Appendices A–D contain no additional display equations; only inline math symbols appear.)

## The Loss Function

**Equation (2)** in Section 3.2 (Training) is the loss function. It is the **negative log-likelihood loss** used to train the dual-encoder retriever:

$$L(q_i, p_i^+, p_{i,1}^-, \ldots, p_{i,n}^-) = -\log \frac{e^{\operatorname{sim}(q_i, p_i^+)}}{e^{\operatorname{sim}(q_i, p_i^+)} + \sum_{j=1}^{n} e^{\operatorname{sim}(q_i, p_{i,j}^-)}}$$

This is a standard cross-entropy / InfoNCE-style contrastive loss where, given a positive passage p_i⁺ and n negative passages, the model maximizes the similarity of the question to the positive passage relative to the negatives.
